newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs trade narrowly ahead of tankan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs trade narrowly ahead of tankan.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures slipped in thin trade on Thursday driven mainly by technicals, dealers said.
Many participants chose to wait out U.S. international trade data later Thursday, the weekend Group of Seven (G7) summit and Bank of Japan's tankan business sentiment survey, due June 25.
"The mood is still positive, that there will not be interest rate tightening in Japan, but people will move only after the tankan report," a dealer with a Japanese brokerage said.
December Euroyen stood at 99.08 at 1200 GMT after trading a 99.08-99.11 range against an IMM close at 99.10.
A growing belief the tankan would paint a negative business outlook, thus keeping interest rates unchanged, gave euroyen an upward bias, dealers said.
The nearby months were deemed to have reached their peaks, but some felt there could be upside after the report.
"Range-trading will continue for both Euroyen and JGB's. They will consolidate before attempting higher for now," another dealer with a European commission house said.
September JGBs slipped to close around session lows at 123.96, against the previous day's 124.05. Dealers said the fall was merely technical and not reflective of the cash market.
Investors were seen profit taking after several days of gains, especially as the topside around 124.20 appeared heavy.
Eurodollar futures ended barely changed on a lack of incentives and tame U.S. consumer inflation data recently.
Expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would delay a hike in short-term rates until year end also dulled trading.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.960, unchanged from their IMM close while March settled at 93.88 against 93.89.
